main_body: A flat ground patch of green grass texture (named 'desert') filling the whole 64x48 area. It is a terrain tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none; a flat repeating grass texture with no top or front structure
evidence: Terrain ground patch with no standing volume. The column scan shows only a repeating pattern of green speckle rows (L 85-170) with no top/front structure, so the 3/4 contract does not apply. The terrain kind matches. Note the name 'desert' does not match the green grass look, but the kind is still ground terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile, against 80 colours and 26 per tile for the grass reference. It has 4 green steps in a visibly repeating dot pattern: the same clump motif tiles every 16px, which looks mechanical. There are no flat fills (0% coverage) and no neutral outlines. The texture is a regular stipple, much thinner than the grass reference's varied tufts and soil grain. Paving has a similar colour count (7), but it is a different material, and grass is the closer match for a ground patch. Density is well below the grass reference, so it fails.
